learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and capacities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Identifies problems where it is necessary to apply the equations of Deformable Solid Mechanics. Manages the concepts of stress, strain, and behavior models.

Understands the meaning of stress and strain tensors and must be able to express these tensors in different reference systems, including the principal system, and know the importance of principal stresses and directions.
Identifies and applies material behavior models (linear elastic, non-linear elastic, inelastic, etc.) from experimental stress-strain curves.

Knows how to apply the basic equations of Elasticity. The student must be able to formulate the equations of the mathematical model: equilibrium, constitutive, and compatibility at different levels (point, element, and structure) and analytically solve simple problems.
Knows the necessary methodology to solve the elastic problem using finite elements and uses FE software, identifying and selecting the type of finite element.
Knows how to assess the admissibility of analytical and numerical results.
Establishes the limit states of elastic behavior: large deformations, plasticity, instability, etc.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Linear Elastic Solid Mechanics
Differential formulation of the elastic problem
Formulation of FEM in plane elasticity
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes: Develop the scientific body and present application examples.
Practical problem-solving classes: Allow students to apply concepts to solve engineering practice problems.
Computer simulation practicals: Familiarize students with another basic tool for numerical calculation and simulation.
Tutorials: Allow, in a more individualized way or through small groups, students to integrate the various contents and consolidate the object of their learning.
assessment_rules: The course can be passed via continuous or global evaluation. Continuous evaluation includes practices (20%) and two partial exams (80%), each with a minimum score of 4.5/10. Global evaluation comprises a final exam (85%) with a minimum of 4.5/10 per block and a practice exam (15%) with a minimum of 5/10. In both cases, the final weighted average must exceed 5/10. The second call (resit) uses global evaluation, and students must prove authorship of all submitted work; unauthorized use of materials during evaluation may lead to exam withdrawal and a score of '0'.
